verdicts.rewritten_summary: National-framework item (applies to Madhya Pradesh): India's parliament passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill on 25 March 2026 amid protests in Mumbai. If assented, it removes the 2014 self-identification right, limits legal recognition to historically accepted categories (traditional communities and intersex people), mandates medical certification, and adds offences carrying up to life imprisonment for 'coercing or alluring' people to be transgender — amending the 2019 law. The rights group People's Union for Civil Liberties warns the offences echo colonial-era criminalisation of transgender people.

National-framework item (applies to Madhya Pradesh): BBC coverage of the same bill India's parliament passed in March 2026, approved by both houses and awaiting presidential assent. It ends the 2014 Supreme Court self-identification right, narrows recognition to male/female categories plus traditional identities, and makes medical-board and district-authority certification mandatory for gender-affirming surgery. Critics warn the narrower definition excludes self-identifying gender-fluid and non-binary people; ~2 million transgender people live in India.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Framework item for German Länder, incl. Baden-Württemberg: Verfassungsblog analysis (18 Mar 2026) of prison placement for trans prisoners. Placement rules in most Länder were unchanged since the 1970s and are being revised: since 1 March 2026 a new Art. 17 of Rhineland-Palatinate's prison law is in force, with Bavarian, Saxon and Hamburg rules also recently entering into force — giving a majority of Länder revised rules. The piece argues there is no constitutional duty to anchor placement to the registered gender entry (a prisoner self-declaration would intrude less on the right to gender self-determination), and notes only Bremen's law explicitly references the gender entry while others do so implicitly. Baden-Württemberg is not named: its own prison law retains the unrevised 1970s-era placement rules.
